questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I chose my destination, I was seeking a place that would provide me with fruitful knowledge at the hospital, but also a city that would provide me with plenty of things to do during the weekends. I was also looking for contrasts from what I am used to - both culturally, gastronomically, climate-wise and within the medical field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: So and so, the majority of the information that I needed for the paperwork prior to my arrival was provided by my sending institution, which was a big help. However, I still needed to have an overview over, what I need to submit at which dates and who I needed to contact to get these documents and information. Sometimes it would be unclear exactly which type of documents and information that I needed to fill out in different schemes (for instance the OLA), but both my sending institution and my host university was very good at responding within reasonable time frames.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assigned an ESN buddy from the host university, got invited to the big ESN-group chat on WhatsApp and from the Erasmus office I got some information about where to show up and what to bring for my first day at the hospital.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was overall semi-satisfied with the orientation. During my stay, I could always write to Stella and she would get quite rapidly back with a response. However, I would have appreciated some more orientation about where to go for my surgical rotation -  I just found a department myself and showed up there, which also worked nicely, but also a bit of a homemade solution.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is overall quite easy to find housing off campus. The only thing that is difficult, is finding housing that isn’t overpriced. Many people seek housing via AirBnB, which is very convenient and transparent, but the prices are targeted tourists. In the beginning, I lived by Ammoudara in an AirBnB, which I wasn’t satisfied with; the rent being high and the location not working for me, as the last bus from the city center to Amoudara would leave around 22/23 - meaning being social in the city center was difficult. Therefore, I reached out to my ESN buddy who helped me with finding more central and cheaper housing - from this point it all worked out; I got a central apartment for a reasonable, still quite high rent. I can recommend highly living in the city center.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is the most common solution amongst Erasmus students. You will have most of the social gatherings within walking distance. There goes busses quite frequently to the hospital and the university - this can take anywhere from 20-45 minutes depending on traffic, so be in good time.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I got nominated by my sending university, I filled out an online application form in which I applied for courses and filled out some personal information about myself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The erasmus-coordinator Stella Melina was good at answering my mails, when questions appeared.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the clinical courses at the hospital that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have an overview over the deadlines and documents you need for the registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the theoretical aspect of the clinical rotations was quite high, due to the cases being quite complicated - sometimes details would be lost due to language barrier. The opportunity to practice procedures, such as NG-tubes, arterial punctures and urinary catheters was also nice - but it does demand that you show initiative. I do recommend showing the log book as early on as possible.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The greek style of teaching at the hospital is pr default more observational and less interactive than what we know from UCPH. However, I did figure that showing initiative and interest opened a lot more doors for being involved with the patients and getting more responsibilities in the clinic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical clerkship in internal medicine
Clinical clerkship in surgery

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did 5 weeks in the vascular surgery department - I would highly recommend this for future students also. The doctors are passionate about teaching, translating and involving you.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I purchased my own scrubs for the hospital, since the hospital did not provide me with these.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in general was cheaper than expected - specifically the food at the tavernas was cheaper; this enabled me to have weekly dinners out on restaurants and still sticking to my budget. Also many attractions were free entrance, which often meant that you just had to pay for the transportation to that given attraction. Furthermore more expensive items include cosmetics and dairy products such as milk and greek yoghurt

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every month we would recieve a calendar with these kind of activies from ESN comittee. Amongst the cultural activities could be wine tasting, cooking classes, cretan festivals and trips to other cities. Out of the athletic activities, hikes, cretan dance classes and volleyball tournaments were offered. In terms of social activities, there was arranged a whole welcome week with many icebreakers and socializing events, during the stay there was also offered events such as escape rooms and paintball.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the cultural events - specifically the clean Monday event, where we went to a local village and got traditional greek barbecque and wine. I enjoyed this because it was probably my most authentic experience. But I really did enjoy all the non-academic activities that I participated in.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
As an erasmus you get 50% off ferries - I highly recommend this; I went to Milos, Paros, Naxos and Santorini. All of these were stunning. 
On the island of Crete, I recommend exploring Sitia, Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania. The south side is also beautiful and great for camping and hiking. In terms of hiking, there are many good trails and gorges.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy. Cretans are used to having new faces around and are very polite and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The hospital is truly a great place to create bonds with the locals - they are curious on you and are very helpful with all the questions you might have.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t really find any cultural differences challenging - they were just interesteing to me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The greek warmth, both temperature-wise and amongst the people and the greek gastronomy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go to the hospital canteen at lunch time; the food is free and you will meet many other nice erasmus students.
- Bring your own sunscreen and scrubs.
- Enjoy! Time goes crazy fast and this stay is truly magical.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is free lunch for all Erasmus students at the hospital from 13:30 (located at the gamma-section of the hospital - only available if you are on clinical rotation).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting close friendships from several parts of the world, exploring Greece together and exchanging our cultures with each other.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studying, going to the clinical rotations, psychical activity, social gatherings and getting rest. Many great opportunities on this island and it can be overwhelming from time to time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
